title: 暈…這年頭還有說人話的AI不
abstract: 暈…這年頭還有說人話的AI不 衡宇 2026-10-07 16:41:13 來源： 量子位 Jay發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 不er，只有我一個人看不懂AI現在的說話方式了嗎？ 早上起來開啟Claude，美美驗收昨晚的Vibe Coding成果，結果差點沒兩眼一黑暈死過去。 賬本15/15全綠、單腿啞火、同波大刪除…… ？？？ 啥玩意兒啊，這還是中文嗎？？ 本來以為是自己智商有問題，跟不上節奏了，結果在網上逛了一圈後發現，原來大家都這樣。 天下苦「不言人語」久矣，到處都是Fable的吐槽帖。 有對程式碼底座不滿意，要換皮子的。 有剛從備忘錄回來，馬上就在終端視窗原地生產的。 甚至驗屍官都整出來了，要來程式碼庫抓殭屍，生化危機這一塊。 △圖源：小紅書@Yusenthebot 力竭了。 如果你是來自古代的穿越者，不管是秦朝、唐朝還是哪個朝—— 歡迎。 全球AI表達能力集體倒退兩千年 ，我們重新進入文言文紀元了。 AI古語鑑賞 這是前段時間在全球開發者身上每日上演的慘案。 無論是Fable還是Sol還是其他模型，但凡和Coding沾上一點關係， 沒一個能說人話了 。 單獨每個字都能讀得明白，但拼在一塊—— 15/15全綠，再給你加幾條鐵律和紅線與你對拍。 太可怕了，為什麼AI要和我對拍。 還有它到底要把誰的皮重新揉一揉o(╥﹏╥)o。 前所未聞的黑話，還以為是哪家新成立的大廠。 不過，也有網友表示：沒那麼玄乎，單純是翻譯的問題。 像「單腿啞火」這類表達，原意基本就是one leg is dead，程式設計語境下很正常，開發者經常把互為備份或並行的兩條路徑叫leg。 有道理… 但老愛咬人是個啥情況啊？？？ 我現在都不敢認真讀AI的交付彙報，太驚為天人了，生怕一不注意，自己的語料庫也15/15全綠。 求求了，少刷點Coding Bench，回來重新做圖靈測試吧。 好在模型廠也是意識到這個問題了。 最新的Opus 5.5就很讓人欣慰，語言能力回升了非常多， 基本不咋說黑話了 。 但我還是最愛Opus 4.6啊！！ 全中了穴居人的詭計 為啥會這樣？ Coding過擬合當然是一個主要因素，但之前在YouTube也看過另一種分析，說是CoT的影響可能更大。 為了減少Token消耗，模型廠商故意把AI的思考過程，調成了山頂洞語 。 OpenAI應該是最早這麼幹的。 雖然GPT的思維鏈是隱藏的，但幾個月之前，有開發者偶然間開到了盲盒。 大概長下面這樣。 雖然也能看懂啥意思，但反正是徹底不言人語，不影響意義傳遞的詞全囫圇吞棗了。 但這也是OpenAI一直比A/算力夠用的原因之一，穴居人的推理效率高的嚇人。 同樣的一句話，穴居人的 Token消耗量比白話文整整少了70% 。 其實吧，Claude很長一段時間都是用自然語言風格做的思維鏈，直到Opus 4.6之後，也屈服了，自此開始不言人語。 如今V4 Pro也成了受害者。。。 Need to identify as DeepSeek model. The system says You are DeepSeek, knowledge cutoff May 2025, current date Aug 2026. We need be honest. We are DeepSeek latest model? 沒辦法，算力真的不夠啊，別說模型廠了，甚至使用者都被調成了穴居人。 GitHub有個專門的Skill，就叫CaveMan，專門教AI不說人話。 很早之前就火了一次，現在熱度還是很恐怖，都 104K星星 了。 思路就一句話： 能用一個字的，絕不用兩個字。 看到這我一愣。 你等等…按照這思路發展，你如果搞成中文版…… 那不就是文言文嗎？？？ 直接翻開《論語》，你看這精煉的文言文，多節省Token。 子曰：三人行，必有我師焉。擇其善者而從之，其不善者而改之。 孔子說：幾個人在一起行走，其中必定有可作為我的老師的人，要選擇他們的長處來學習，如果看到他們的缺點要反省自己有沒有像他們一樣的缺點，若有，要一起加以改正…… 亦有眾網友早已躬身試之於Vibe Coding，皆稱其善：蓋能省費頗多矣，善哉善哉。 （bushi） 更搞笑的是有人在評論區艾特Grok—— 評之。 老馬親兒子也給出了高度評價。 那還說啥了，善哉善哉，快把我高中語文課本找出來！ 你別笑，我找了圈，發現還真有科學依據啊。 網友Susan STEM表示： 中文 ，尤其是 文言文 ，是人類歷史上少有的、甚至可以說是唯一在非計算機時代被系統性壓縮過的自然語言。 ？？你別說，還真是啊。 中文本來就是獨一份的象形文字系統。一個字，往往就是一整個概念，一整個動作。字即語義，天生就比拼音文字省地方。 何況為了在竹簡上多寫點字，老祖宗們還在這基礎上又壓縮了一道，搞出了文言文。 主語、助詞大幅縮減，連語序也幫你焊死了。 別的語言當然也講究，拉丁語、古希臘語、梵文、阿拉伯語，各有各的精緻。 但它們講究的是音義準，是語法美。 真沒哪一種，像中文這樣，被當成一門「壓縮工程」，認認真真搞了幾千年。 簡直是天選AI母語啊。 然後我又往前翻了翻，發現個更令人癱軟的真相。 2019年，真有人把文言文，直接寫成了一門程式語言 。 專案叫「文言」（wenyan-lang），作者黃令東（Lingdong Huang），當時還是CMU一個搞計算機加藝術交叉的學生。 一發布直接炸了，GitHub如今已經 20K星 。 你沒看錯，完全按照文言文的文體和語氣來設計的，字元表裡只有繁體中文和「」引號。 你把這類程式碼原樣丟回幾千年前，孔子都能看得懂。 舉個例子，Hello World。 吾有一言。曰「「天地，好在否！」」。書之。 機器的輸出就是，「同天地好在」。 來來來，誰說中文邏輯性不如英文的！ 這還學個啥蘇格拉底提問法啊。。。 太領先了奧，敢情老祖宗們才是史上第一 提示詞工程師 。 我宣佈，所有高校中文系明年原地漲50分！ （bushi） One More Thing 所以，說了這麼多，如今究竟還有說人話的的AI嗎？ 還真有。。。 你谷歌的哈基米，秒了 。 （PS. 左邊是你基米哥，右側為「不是而是」大師GPT） 原來我智商是正常的，原來我不是 ADHD 。 說實話，平時網上罵罵就算了，真日常聊天，誰不想急頭白臉地開啟Gemini，猛猛聽基米哥諂媚一番啊。 用來最佳化Skill也是神了，寫作SOTA這一塊，完全不會往番茄炒蛋里加東坡肉。 反觀GPT給我寫的，簡直跟加密文件一樣。。。 全球AI表達能力下降一百倍，唯你基米哥巋然不動o(╥﹏╥)o。 當然Coding能力還有智商也是一如既往的巋然不動。 所以究竟是為啥呢？？ 語言風格當然是一方面，但我覺得，排版也是個非常重要的變數。 Gemini模型輸出的視覺層級做得極好，縮排塊、斜體、無序列表、留白……甚至左側還有一條貫穿的輔助線。 這些本身就能去除噪音，提供更清晰的訊號。 還是挺有意思的，UI層藏了不少小設計。 感覺最近社群風評也出現了不少轉向，之前不管谷歌發個啥東西，評論區馬上就被衝爛了。 上週Gemini 3.8 Flash，居然有不少人幫基米哥說話，說基米哥是唯一還能溝通的AI。 也是神了。 Coding大戰打了這麼久，模型參數一路從幾百B漲到10T。 結果最後唯一還能說人話的—— 竟然只剩下了美國豆包 。 （注：咳咳，不指Gemini 4 Argon） title: Meshy 躋身 a16z 消費級 AI 應用月收入 Top 50，為榜單唯一 AI 3D 公司
abstract: Meshy 躋身 a16z 消費級 AI 應用月收入 Top 50，為榜單唯一 AI 3D 公司 量子位的朋友們 2026-10-07 14:39:36 來源： 量子位 在 a16z 首份消費級 AI 應用月收入榜單中，Meshy 位列第 31 名，與 OpenAI、Anthropic、Canva、Superhuman、Higgsfield 等共同上榜 加州矽谷，2026 年 10 月 5 日 —— 全球領先的 AI 3D 多模態模型公司 Meshy 今日宣佈，公司入選由矽谷風險投資機構 Andreessen Horowitz（a16z）釋出的“消費級 AI 應用月收入Top 50”榜單。Meshy 位列第 31 名，是榜單上唯一一家 AI 3D 公司，與 OpenAI、Anthropic、Canva、Superhuman、Higgsfield 等企業共同上榜。 該榜單今日隨 a16z 第七版《百強AI消費者應用》報告一同釋出。這份報告是觀察消費級 AI 市場最受關注的風向標之一。以往幾版報告均按網站訪問量和移動端活躍度為 AI 產品排名，本版首次新增收入榜單，依據資料分析公司 YipitData 追蹤的美國消費者銀行卡消費資料，更清晰地揭示出消費者真正願意為哪些 AI 產品付費。 a16z 在報告中指出，收入榜單上多款頭部創意類產品均建立在自研模型之上；即便通用模型在影像和影片生成方面不斷進步，消費者仍持續為專業化創意工具付費。Meshy 自主研發面向 3D 生成的多模態模型，此次上榜標誌著 AI 3D 已經和語言、影像、影片、音樂一樣，成為一個獨立的付費品類。 “很榮幸 Meshy 成為該榜單上唯一的 AI 3D 公司，這說明 3D 已經成為使用者願意付費的品類。”Meshy 增長副總裁潘菲表示，“每天，都有大量藝術家、工作室和創作者藉助 Meshy，在幾分鐘內把創意變成 3D 作品。我們相信，3D 將是下一個偉大的創作媒介，而我們的使命，就是讓每個人都能輕鬆用 3D 進行創作。” 此次入選，是 Meshy 一段快速增長期的縮影。公司近期宣佈，其年度經常性收入（ARR）已突破 1 億美元；2026 年 7 月，公司完成近 4 億美元 B 輪融資，投後估值超 100 億元。 關於 Meshy Meshy 構建用於 AI 驅動 3D 生成的多模態基礎模型，將文本和影像轉化為可用於遊戲、電影和 3D 列印的生產級 3D 資產。Meshy 由擁有麻省理工學院博士學位的胡淵鳴（Ethan Hu ）創立，目前在全球擁有超過 1500 萬註冊使用者。2026 年 7 月，該公司完成了近 4 億美元的 B 輪融資，估值達 15 億美元，這是迄今為止 AI 3D 領域最大的融資輪次。瞭解更多資訊，請訪問 meshy.ai。 本文由Meshy提供，量子位獲授權轉載，觀點歸原作者所有。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Meshy 量子位的朋友們 《怪物史萊克》編劇也來了！這家AI影視公司，影片模型全球第二！ 2026-10-07 國產世界模型首次出海上路！Momenta直接讓百億公里老司機開上歐洲街頭 2026-09-30 正行創新聯合創始人楊宇欣正式亮相：出任總裁，負責全球業務拓展 2026-09-29 DeepSeek知乎獨家發文，首次公開V4.1 Agent訓練“大本營”DSec 2026-09-30 相關閱讀

title: OpenAI一夜甩出722篇數學論文！黎曼霍奇BSD全上陣，數學家：讀不過來
abstract: OpenAI一夜甩出722篇數學論文！黎曼霍奇BSD全上陣，數學家：讀不過來 聽雨 2026-10-07 09:05:13 來源： 量子位 三位菲爾茲獎得主：不代表認可 聽雨 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 剛剛，OpenAI往數學界扔了顆重磅炸彈—— 一口氣公開 722篇數學手稿 ，全部出自一個還沒釋出的內部模型。 這些手稿歸成372組結果。據OpenAI介紹，模型此前一共嘗試了約4000個研究問題，平均每項結果消耗的算力，約相當於ChatGPT Pro思考3小時。 論文、原始碼、部分Lean證明，被一股腦傳上了GitHub。 翻開目錄， 準黎曼猜想、霍奇猜想、BSD猜想、π的無理性指數 ……一個比一個名頭大。 光是千禧難題，就沾上了三道。 再往下翻，還有自旋玻璃、量子磁性、自由群因子、相對論性弗拉索夫—麥克斯韋方程……數論、代數幾何、理論計算機、統計力學，17個方向鋪得滿滿當當。 一夜之間，數學論文堆成了山。 數學家們看了直呼：這誰讀得完啊…… 722篇手稿裡，究竟寫了什麼？ 點開GitHub倉庫，先看到一份巨巨巨長的目錄。 有的組只有一篇主論文，有的還附了另一種證明、相關推論。除了論文PDF和原始碼，倉庫裡還有10份模型推理摘要。 最搶眼的，恐怕是第003組： 「準黎曼猜想」 。 黎曼猜想要證明，黎曼ζ函式的非平凡零點全都落在實部為1/2的直線上。 OpenAI給出的結論是： ζ函式和所有狄利克雷L函式，在實部大於7/8的區域都沒有零點 。 這個結論有多猛？ 此前，數學家連「實部大於0.99的一整條豎帶裡沒有零點」都證不出來，已知的無零點區域，只是貼著實部=1的邊緣越收越窄。 也就是說，它聲稱一口氣把零點可能出現的範圍往中間推了一大截。當然，離黎曼猜想要求的那條1/2直線，還有距離。 而且同組裡還不止一份證明。另一份獨立證明給出的是實部大於11/12的版本，範圍稍窄，但多帶了一個結論：一致排除「西格爾零點」。 西格爾零點，指的是某些L函式可能藏在實數1附近的“搗亂零點”。它們是否存在，困擾了數論學家近百年，許多關於素數分佈的結果，都得繞開它們寫。 緊接著是第004組， 有理數域上的希爾伯特第十問題 ： 拿到一個整數係數的多項式，能否寫出一套通用演算法，判斷它有沒有有理數解？ OpenAI給出的結論是，這樣的演算法不存在。 這道題的整數版本，1970年就由蘇聯數學家馬季亞謝維奇最終解決；有理數版本卻懸了半個多世紀。 再來是另一道千禧難題： 伯奇和斯溫納頓-戴爾猜想 ，也就是 BSD猜想 。 它把橢圓曲線上有理點的情況，和一個相關函式在特定位置的表現聯絡起來。 OpenAI聲稱，針對滿足Selmer餘秩為0或1等條件的橢圓曲線，得到了完整公式；再結合倉庫裡的另一組結果，按密度統計，可覆蓋每條有理數域上橢圓曲線的絕大多數二次扭曲。 第三道千禧難題，是 霍奇猜想 。 這道題關心的是，一類複雜幾何空間裡看得見的「形狀資訊」，能否由代數方程定義出的幾何物件來解釋。 OpenAI這組手稿處理的是兩類物件：具有特殊復乘結構的阿貝爾簇，以及K3曲面的乘積。 其中關於復乘阿貝爾簇的論文，聲稱覆蓋了這一類物件的所有維度和餘維。不過霍奇猜想涉及的幾何空間要廣得多，這批論文目前只覆蓋上述範圍。 另外，還有兩個看著像中學數學、實際困擾了許多年的常數問題。 一篇論文聲稱證明， π的無理性指數恰好是2 。 問題在於：用分數逼近π，到底能逼近得多準？ 此前最好的結果，只能把這個指數壓到7.1左右，現在直接壓到了理論最優值2。 另一篇聲稱證明， 卡塔蘭常數是無理數 。π是無理數早有定論；卡塔蘭常數究竟是不是無理數，此前一直沒有公認的證明。 理論電腦科學那邊，還有第102組的 唯一遊戲猜想 。 這道題牽著一串問題：有些複雜的最佳化任務，演算法究竟能把答案逼近到什麼程度？ 這個猜想2002年由Khot提出，2018年數學家證明了它的一個弱化版本，完整版一直沒拿下。 OpenAI在目錄中聲稱證明了這一猜想，還給出了最大割、頂點覆蓋等問題的近似難度結論。 再往下翻，畫風越來越稀奇古怪…… 稀疏自旋玻璃的梅扎爾—帕裡西公式、量子海森堡鐵磁體的自發磁化、自由群因子同構，以及三維單種粒子相對論性弗拉索夫—麥克斯韋方程的整體光滑解，都出現在結果目錄裡。 值得注意的是，OpenAI表示，平均每項結果消耗的算力約相當於ChatGPT Pro思考3小時。 倉庫也交代了：絕大多數結果，都是同一個未釋出的內部模型按同一套固定流程跑出來的。 但有兩項是例外—— **黎曼ζ函式的無零點區域 ，以及 復乘阿貝爾簇上的霍奇猜想** ，沒有完全走這套固定流程。 其中，黎曼ζ函式實部大於11/12的那篇證明，文稿還經過了人工編輯，以便讀者閱讀。 倉庫也寫明瞭，這些手稿的核驗進度各不相同，部分成果還沒有Lean形式化證明。 數學家：No No No！幾百篇手稿誰來讀啊… OpenAI一口氣發了幾百篇數學論文，數學界看起來可不怎麼買帳。 722篇手稿剛上線，由九位學者組成的獨立數學與AI顧問組就發了宣告。 這個顧問組來頭不小，裡面有三位菲爾茲獎得主： Timothy Gowers 、 Martin Hairer ，以及理論物理學家 Edward Witten 。 他們承認，這是數學界的一件大事。但他們同時表示：顧問組此前給OpenAI提過建議， 不代表他們已經認可這些結果，也不代表他們認可OpenAI產出成果的過程 。 證明是否成立、對後續研究有多大用處，要交給各領域的數學家慢慢消化。 手稿釋出前，得克薩斯大學奧斯汀分校數學家 Francesco Maggi 就在社媒上發問： 9月那篇流體力學證明，專家們至今還在研究它究竟怎麼起作用； 一下再來數百篇，誰有精力讀？讀完以後，又能從中發現什麼新方法、新問題？ Maggi的態度很有代表性。他並不反對用AI做數學，但他擔心的是，結果產出的速度已經遠遠超過了人類能理解的速度，數學家只能在後面追著AI跑。 其實，這批手稿釋出前，OpenAI也找數學家專門喝過茶，試圖做做工作。 據WIRED訊息，8月，OpenAI召集約40名數學家，討論成果該怎麼釋出。 西北大學數學家Bryna Kra等人希望看到寫得清楚、能讓同行閱讀和引用的論文。 部分與會者稱，他們當時以為OpenAI不會一次放出所有成果；OpenAI發言人則表示，公司不清楚有過這樣的承諾。 9月的流體力學爭議，又讓氣氛變得更緊張。 當時，NYU數學家Tristan Buckmaster與Anthropic研究員Levent Alpöge公開了三篇流體方程爆破證明，同樣配有Lean形式化。 幾乎同一時間，OpenAI釋出了納維–斯托克斯證明。 Buckmaster表示，原本想再花時間把證明寫得好讀一些，最終因外部壓力提前釋出。 隨後，Buckmaster一方與OpenAI圍繞研究進度和成果歸屬起了爭執，雙方拿出了相近/相同的結果，而OpenAI否認Buckmaster此前使用Codex時的提示詞影響了自己的模型。 就連曾經最愛AI、逢人就安利AI工具的 陶哲軒 ，也忍不住踩剎車了。 9月，他在加州理工的一場演講中說，AI發展的速度「太瘋狂了」，沒有理由這麼快！ AI公司簡直就跟瘋了一樣。 菲爾茲獎得主 Cédric Villani ，在看到OpenAI拿下千禧難題之一的納維–斯托克斯方程後，也直接癱軟了。。。 我大受震撼…… 簡直跟世界末日一樣，這是數學界有史以來從未見過的浩劫。 到了這次釋出，OpenAI把論文、部分Lean證明和推理摘要統統放進了倉庫，還表示會出資辦研討會，幫助數學界研究這些成果。 顧問組的回應則是：材料公開了，接下來該由數學家檢查、講解，再決定哪些結果真正能進入數學研究。 OpenAI已經交卷了，但數學界的閱卷才剛開始… One More Thing 與此同時，OpenAI的「28天挑戰賽」也來到了Day 2。 此前賽博義父Tibo放話： 接下來28天，每天都要給Codex或Work使用者帶來一項明顯改進；哪天沒交出來，就重置使用者的使用額度。 第二天總共釋出了4項更新： 其中最容易感受到的是 Auto-review ：Codex執行長任務時，可以讓另一個AI代理檢查它準備採取的操作，替使用者攔下高風險動作。 現在，通過ChatGPT賬號登入的使用者使用這一功能，不再消耗套餐額度。 另外三項分別面向開發和日常辦公： API付費檔位從五檔簡化為三檔； Meetings外掛可把會議整理成紀要和待辦； 供開發者呼叫的Decisions API開放公測。 參考連結： [1] https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/ [2] https://github.com/openai/math [3] https://agmai.org/ [4] title: 剛剛，諾貝爾物理獎一人獨攬！
abstract: 剛剛，諾貝爾物理獎一人獨攬！ Jay 2026-10-06 18:44:58 來源： 量子位 南極洲甚至有一座高地以他名字命名 Jay 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 剛剛，諾貝爾物理學獎公佈。 這一次沒有任何並列，得主只有一個人，來自美國威斯康星大學麥迪遜分校的 Francis Halzen （弗朗西斯·哈爾岑）。 如果你不知道這個大學，你應該也會知道它有個知名的中國科技網際網路領域的校友—— 拼多多創始人， 黃崢 。 所以，Francis究竟為何獲獎？ 官方是這麼說的： 表彰他對南極冰立方中微子天文臺（IceCube）的決定性貢獻，以及對天體物理起源高能中微子的發現。 具體而言就是，他把南極地下2000多米深處的 1立方公里 純淨冰層，硬生生改造成一臺捕捉宇宙幽靈粒子的 超級望遠鏡 。。。 如今，南極洲甚至有一座高地，就是以他名字命名的，叫做 Halzen Mesa 。 為什麼要在南極深冰裡抓“幽靈”？ 宇宙裡一直有個困擾物理學界百年的終極謎題：那些能量高到離譜的宇宙射線，到底是從哪兒發射出來的？ 宇宙中存在天然的粒子加速器，噴射出的質子能量比地球實驗室裡最強加速器還要高出上百萬倍。但質子帶電荷，在宇宙裡飛奔時會被星際磁場扭得七葷八素，等落到地球，根本沒人能分清它來自哪個方向。 怎麼才能找到真正的源頭？ 物理學家把目光投向了中微子。 中微子是宇宙中最害羞的粒子，不帶電、質量微乎其微。每秒鐘都有 650億個 來自太陽的中微子穿過你的大拇指指甲蓋，你卻完全感覺不到。 高能質子加速的地方往往會伴生高能中微子。中微子不帶電，不受磁場干擾，也不會被星際塵埃阻擋，就像一根筆直的標靶，直接指向宇宙深處的發源地。 但怎麼抓它呢？ 中微子偶爾會跟原子核撞上，產生帶電粒子併發出極其微弱的藍光。只要介質足夠透明、體積足夠大，就能用光敏感測器把它的軌跡記錄下來。 深海雖然透明，但裡面有活蹦亂跳的生物發光，還有洋流乾擾。Halzen在1980年代提出了一個大膽的想法：去南極，用天然冰層！ 用熱水融出2.5公里深井，造出1立方公里冰下巨眼 在冰天雪地的南極抓粒子，聽起來像天方夜譚。 南極深處的冰層完全處於黑暗之中，沒有海洋生物搗亂，地質結構極其穩定，沒有地震干擾。唯一讓人頭大的問題是：在兩千多米厚的冰川裡，怎麼把感測器塞進去？ 研究團隊想出了一個極其硬核的辦法——用特製的高溫熱水鑽頭，把南極冰層融出一條條深達兩千多米的深孔，然後把掛滿光敏感測器的電纜迅速沉入冰水裡。 Halzen把這些感測器形容為反向燈泡：它們不負責發光，只負責捕捉微弱的光訊號並轉化為電訊號。 早期的先導實驗AMANDA剛啟動時，大家心裡都在打鼓。淺層冰裡全是微小氣泡，光線一打進去就被散射得七零八落。 但當鑽頭下潛到 1400米 以下時，神了——高壓把氣泡全部壓碎擠出，下面的冰層純淨透明到令人驚歎。中微子碰撞產生的藍光，在冰裡甚至能傳播 300米 遠才被吸收！ 驗證可行後，IceCube正式開工。 到2011年完工時，整個IceCube已經深埋在南極冰下 1450到2450米 之間，由 86根電纜 、 5160個光學感測器 組成，把整整 1立方公里 的天然冰川變成了一臺史無前例的中微子望遠鏡。 捕獲宇宙幽靈，開啟天文學全新大門 有了這臺巨型望遠鏡，尋找來自深空的訊號依然像大海撈針。 每天有超過上億個來自南極上方大氣的宇宙射線粒子穿過探測器，還有數百個來自地球另一端大氣的中微子穿透地殼而來。 要在海量背景噪音裡篩選出真正來自遙遠宇宙的高能中微子，資料處理難度太恐怖了。 2013年 ，IceCube團隊終於宣佈，首次明確捕捉到了來自太陽系以外的高能宇宙中微子。這項突破直接拿下了當年的《Physics World》年度突破大獎。 隨後幾年裡，關鍵證據接連出現： 科學家在活躍星系 NGC 1068 （M77）方向記錄到了79箇中微子候選訊號，鎖定了潛在的極端天體源頭。 2023年，IceCube團隊首次繪製出了銀河系平面的高能中微子影像，讓人類第一次透過中微子這雙眼睛看到了銀河系的全貌。 天文學在經歷可見光、射電、X射線、引力波之後，高能中微子天文學的大門被徹底推開了。 諾獎得主其人：從強子物理到冰下造望遠鏡 這位單人獨攬諾貝爾物理學獎的物理學家Francis Halzen，今年82歲。 他1944年出生於比利時蒂嫩，1969年在比利時魯汶大學（KU Leuven）獲得博士學位，早年主要研究夸克構成的重粒子和強子物理中的對稱性破缺。 完成博士後研究後，他前往美國威斯康星大學麥迪遜分校，並從1972年起長期在此任教，擔任物理系教授。 他與他人合著的經典教材《Quarks and Leptons》，陪伴了全球幾代粒子物理學子的成長。 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Jay 高通All in title: 不er，咋陶哲軒也成AI減速派了？？
abstract: 不er，咋陶哲軒也成AI減速派了？？ 林, 方舟 2026-10-06 15:59:17 來源： 量子位 Jay 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 不er，陶哲軒咋成AI減速派了？？ 是的，就是那個曾經最愛AI、逢人就安利AI工具的男人， 一夜之間，漂移到了AI數學的對立面。。。 SAIR最新演講，陶哲軒正式向模型公司開火： 簡直是瘋了，AI公司無休止地加速，卻對那之後會發生什麼一無所知。 必須慢下來。完全沒理由這麼快，一點理由都沒有。 更關鍵的是，感受到危機的，遠不止陶哲軒一人。 而且陶哲軒還算反應比較淡定的。 你的菲爾茲獎得主 Cédric Villani ，在看到OpenAI拿下千禧難題後，直接癱軟了。。。 我大受震撼…… 簡直跟世界末日一樣，這是數學界有史以來從未見過的浩劫。 但我往前翻了下發現，僅僅在3個月前，這哥們對AI的態度還是嗤之以鼻啊。 LLM根本沒有智慧，連洗車問題都會答錯，只不過是統計學復讀機。 洪水是一視同仁的。 面對光速迭代的大模型，即便站在人類智慧金字塔尖的天才數學家們，也終於感受到了核彈爆炸的威力。 （bushi） 從擁抱到謹慎 太魔幻了家人們。 要知道，就在幾個月前，陶哲軒還是最受矽谷推崇的「AI課代表」—— 查文獻、寫程式碼、畫示意圖到輔助計算……早早把AI嵌入了自己的科研工作流。 也特別願意給大家分享自己的方法論，以及最近擁抱AI的感悟和心得。 2026年3月，他在IPAM會議上公開呼籲同行別太死板，稱當前AI在數學和理論物理領域已經 “ready for primetime” ，能省去大量的無用功。 同月接受《MIT科技評論》專訪時，陶哲軒更是興奮地斷言： 數學正經歷一場哥白尼革命。 今年春節前，我們也採訪過陶哲軒。當時他有句話讓我印象特別深刻： 未來，甚至連初中生都能借助AI+Lean的方式，對數學前沿研究做出貢獻。 在陶哲軒那時的藍圖裡，數學將迎來一次前所未有的創造力井噴，未來一片光明。 結果半年過去，畫風突變。 SAIR最新演講中，陶哲軒直接公開喊話模型公司： 別解數學問題了。 這又不是啥世界危機，慢一點！ 陶哲軒最新演講 所以，陶哲軒究竟在反對些什麼？ AI幫人類把幾百年沒解開的世紀難題做出來了，難道不是天大的好事嗎？ 關於這點，陶哲軒打了一個比喻，非常精妙—— 未解決的數學問題就像燈塔。 大多數人出海不是為了燈塔所在的地方，但燈塔是照亮了整片海域與地貌，讓人們能夠安全航行。 長期以來，公眾普遍認為數學家的職責就是解決困難的數學猜想。 但解決了又有啥用呢？ 基本沒啥直接的實用價值，治不了癌症、攻克不了核聚變…… 相比醫學、能源專業，數學可以說相當是純粹的基礎研究了，完全由人類的好奇心驅動。 無論是給孩子出的思考題，還是千禧難題，它們本身，從來不是終點。 真正珍貴的是，是在研究問題的過程中，沿途建立起來的工具、理論框架和洞見。 陶哲軒表示，一個數學證明正常的完整生命週期，通常有五個環節： 提出解答：未經驗證的提議 機械驗證：形式化證明語言如Lean檢查通過 闡釋工作：把生硬的推導翻譯成人能看懂的語言 同行評審：大家一起消化，成為整個行業的共識 寫入教科書：融會貫通，啟發下一代學生 看到問題所在了嗎？ AI模型如今在第一步「生成解答」和第二步「Lean形式化驗證」上瘋狂加速，但後面三步—— 理解、消化、寫教科書，進度幾乎為零啊。。。 AI在不停地碾壓重大猜想，但沒有任何人做報告，沒有人寫論文。 甚至連按下回車鍵生成證明的人，都搞不明白剛剛發生了什麼。 結果就是一場前所未有的知識擁堵。 人類突然生產出大量證明，卻沒有人理解，沒有人發表，沒有人解釋。 這就像20世紀初的交通狀況：原有的街道是為行人和馬車設計的，汽車突然被發明並直接湧入同一條街道，結果造成了全面的擁堵與癱瘓。 陶哲軒稱之為Proof Indigestion（證明消化不良）。 但陶哲軒補充道，這可能也不是模型公司的本意，他們想幹也沒辦法。 AI做不了洞見，因為洞見不可驗證，刷不了分，很難被當做目標函式訓練。 但說實話，我尋思，人類理解不了好像也沒啥關係吧？ AI公司做它的題，數學家繼續埋頭做研究，不管怎麼說發展速度肯定會比之前快。 但陶哲軒指出，長此以往，這會埋下巨大的隱患—— 1、智子危機，數學家創造力喪失。 新的數學問題與前沿方向，往往誕生於撰寫教材體系時的查漏補缺，或是人類在漫長思考與摸索過程中的偶然發現。 AI 呢？直接跳向最終答案，徹底抹殺了這種漫步式探索所帶來的偶發靈感與新領悟。 2、資料汙染 。 現在的AI為什麼數學這麼厲害？因為它們吞噬了人類幾個世紀以來寫在教科書裡的精華，那些被無數數學家反覆打磨、消化透徹的高質量資料。 不過，如果未來整個學術界充斥著海量AI生成、人類無法理解的證明，下一代AI再去吃這些資料訓練，會發生什麼？ 沒人知道。 生物學裡有個著名的「克隆小鼠」故事。 用體細胞克隆出一隻小鼠，再用這隻克隆小鼠的細胞繼續克隆，一代一代往下克隆…… 但問題是，克隆技術本身就有損耗 —— 每次克隆，端粒縮短、表觀遺傳印記丟失、體細胞突變累積等問題都會疊加。 迭代代數越多，這些缺陷積累得越嚴重，最終後代會出現發育異常、存活率下降，甚至根本活不下來。 這也是為什麼陶哲軒覺得，AI公司就這樣一股腦把證明丟出來，非常不負責任。 我們必須慢下來。這個速度太瘋狂了，完全沒有理由這麼快，一點理由都沒有。 而關於陶哲軒的態度轉變，其實也早已草蛇灰線。 一直有在討論AI數學相關風險，只不過被OpenAI「截胡」千禧難題這茬一搞，終於將問題擺到了臺前—— 親自牽頭成立「復仇者聯盟」（bushi）、聯合Peter Scholze、鄧煜以及Pierre Deligne等 25位菲爾茲獎得主 聯名寫了一封公開信，炮轟OpenAI等模型公司。 菲爾茲獎得主 聯名寫了一封公開信大致意思就是說，AI公司不能把數學打benchmark刷，這種做法與數學界追求的目標，是嚴重錯位的。 數學研究真正珍貴的是推導過程中的「認知摩擦」。 光靠大力出奇跡量產True/False ，會毀掉思想生長的土壤。 這之後，陶哲軒又在個人網站上寫了好幾篇部落格，詳細探討過這個問題。 OpenAI回應了 模型公司這邊，也有新動態。 面對25位菲爾茲獎得主的集體抗議，始作俑者OpenAI，終於給出了官方回應—— 宣佈成立一個設在普林斯頓高等研究院（IAS）的獨立顧問小組——「數學與人工智慧顧問小組」（Advisory Group on Mathematics and AI）。 名單陣容極其豪華，包括Edward Witten、Timothy Gowers、Martin Hairer、Melanie Matchett Wood、Camillo De Lellis等一眾數學界與理論物理界的頂級大佬。 OpenAI表示，這個小組將為新興研究成果的審查和傳播提供建議，幫助評估成果的重要性，協調傳播方式。 但是。。。 我仔細看了下OpenAI的官方宣告，發現裡面 白紙黑字寫著這樣一句話 ： 顧問小組將不負責就數學上的內部進展提供建議。 神了。 你可以提建議，可以幫我們PR…… 但想要阻礙我人類之光、模型雙子星OpenAI的IPO之路？ 門都沒有。 當然這是意料之中的，AI公司肯定不會關心咱們的秋招春招。 管你啥數學研究，管你啥菲爾茲獎得主的，都是我IPO的一環，全部跟程式設計師坐一桌去吧！ 不過，我翻了下評論區，發現了一個更有意思的點—— 好像就連網友，也沒啥人共情數學界的啊。。。 全是幸災樂禍的，玩梗玩得不亦樂乎。 AI面前，天才也沒啥特別的。 而最扎心的，莫過於這串靈魂三問—— 畫家倒下時，陶哲軒在哪？ 作家倒下時，陶哲軒在哪？ 程式設計師倒下時，你陶哲軒，又在哪？ 參考連結： [1]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZRb6NIki2w [2]https://t.co/QCMFLFlIv8 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 大模型 數學 林, 方舟 title: OpenAI「瘋狂28天」首日，這都發了些啥啊…
abstract: OpenAI「瘋狂28天」首日，這都發了些啥啊… 林, 方舟 2026-10-06 14:45:40 來源： 量子位 林方舟 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 事情真的有點荒誕。 賽博義父、Codex負責人Tibo昨天剛說完，接下來的28天裡，他們每天要麼交付一項Codex/Work的改進，要麼來一次完整的額度重置。 今天，是Codex“瘋狂28天”的第一天。Tibo興沖沖地跑出來發推宣佈： GPT-6 Astra和GPT-6.1 Sol的預設推理速度提升了約50% 按理說官方發福利、模型大提速，評論區本該是一片歡騰。 結果點開評論區，直接給我整不會了。 清一色的翻車，無人在意提速，滿屏都是網友的冷嘲熱諷。。。 28天“懲罰遊戲”第一天 事情的起因，是Tibo在X上釋出的28天“軍令狀”。 全員重置額度成為了一種“懲罰”，釋出體驗改進成為了“免受懲罰的籌碼”。（doge） 第一天，大家本以為怎麼也得來個重磅炸彈，結果Tibo宣佈的成果是：速度最佳化。。。 按照官方說法，無論是通過官方訂閱，還是用Sign in with ChatGPT接入的第三方生態（比如OpenCode、Pi、Amp、Devin等），GPT-6 Astra和GPT-6.1 Sol的預設推理速度都提速了約50%，達到了50TPS。 這第一刀為啥偏偏砍向了模型速度？ 害，還不是因為之前翻車了嘛。 9月29日，新發布的GPT-6.1 Sol剛一上線，就拉了坨大的。 即便使用者使用Fast模式，模型也巨慢無比。有人吐槽，它應該改名叫：GPT-6.1 Turtle（烏龜）。 Tibo隨後公開道歉，表示GPT-6.1 Sol前兩天遭遇了巨大的負載增長，才導致執行緩慢，並宣佈恢復預期速度、安排付費賬戶額度重置。 接著，Tibo又徵集了一圈網友意見，將接下來的工作鎖定在四個方向： 簡化產品、提高效率以支援更多使用、突破性功能、新模型。 隨後，Tibo正式開啟了“瘋狂28天”計劃。 隔著螢幕我都能感受到Tibo的焦慮：我心愛的使用者們，可千萬別走啊T_T 廣告和水印也安排上了 如果只是更新力度平平，大家或許還只是調侃幾句。 偏偏就在同一時間，OpenAI連續搞了兩個讓打工人和開發者兩眼一黑的騷操作。 一個是 在ChatGPT裡塞廣告 。 官方發文宣佈，每週觸達12億使用者的ChatGPT，將在影像生成過程中，測試全新的視覺廣告形式。 以後你焦急等待模型生圖，介面上直接給你彈出一張贊助商的品牌展示圖，底下還貼心地放著一個“瞭解更多”的跳轉按鈕。 你說你氣不氣ヽ(`Д´)ﾉ title: Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses
abstract: AI agents have evolved from single models to complex full-stack systems built from models, tools, and execution environments. Their capabilities increasingly depend on the agent harness that coordinates them from outside the model. Reinforcement learning (RL) is an approach where AI systems learn through trial and error, guided by rewards and penalties for their actions. RL can make those agents better, but most agent RL systems require developers to reimplement the agent inside the training framework. That is costly, and it means the agent being trained is not quite the agent that gets deployed. To address this, researchers at Microsoft Research Asia have introduced the Harnessed Agentic RL training paradigm and open-sourced a fully rebuilt Agent Lightning v1.0 (opens in new tab) . Compared with the original, Agent Lightning, v1.0 puts more emphasis on staying lightweight, on integrating with real harnesses, and on a complete, reproducible agent RL training pipeline. Agent Lightning v1.0 was rebuilt around Harnessed Agentic RL, with key improvements: Traditional agentic RL assumes the training framework owns the interaction loop with the environment. In a ReAct-style loop, the model generates an action, the environment returns an observation, the observation is appended to the context, and the model generates the next action, so the whole rollout maps onto one continuous token trajectory. Early RL systems such as verl, AReaL, and slime were built this way, which meant training an agent required rebuilding its loop inside the RL framework. Real harnesses have outgrown that assumption. Coding agents such as mini-SWE-agent, OpenHands, OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex each bring their own context management, tool protocols, execution logic, and dependencies, as do general-purpose agent systems. Rebuilding one for training is expensive, and the rebuilt agent may no longer behave in the same way as the deployed agent. Agent Lightning takes a different route. It places an LLM proxy between the agent and the model. The agent continues to run as before: simply point the endpoint that previously called the model API at Agent Lightning, and the training framework can observe and record its model calls. In v1.0, the researchers go further and formally define this paradigm as Harnessed Agentic RL: whichever agent harness is used in deployment is the harness that takes part directly in reinforcement learning during training (Figure 1). A core difference between Harnessed Agentic RL and traditional agentic RL is that the environment interaction loop is handled by the agent harness rather than the training framework. The training system can only observe a series of LLM request and response pairs, so a single rollout may be split into a variable number of training samples. This brings four key challenges: In system design, Agent Lightning v1.0 treats simplicity as its first principle. The entire framework is about 3,500 lines of code, with three core components: the API Gateway, the Rollout Controller, and the Customized Trainer (Figure 2). The API gateway stores rollouts, models, and events, and serves as an OpenAI-compatible LLM proxy. It links every model call from the harness to its rollout and records the prompts, responses, and log probabilities that training needs. The rollout controller starts and manages agent execution, either as local processes or as standard Kubernetes jobs, keeping agent execution separate from the trainer. The customized trainer, built on verl, creates rollouts, waits for them to finish, collects samples, and assembles the final training samples through a sample adapter. As a result, for an existing agent harness, simply pointing the model endpoint at the Agent Lightning proxy is usually enough to connect quickly to RL training. Rollout times vary widely across agents. Synchronous RL waits for the slowest agent in a batch and leaves GPUs idle, while fully asynchronous RL raises utilization but needs separate GPU pools for rollout and training. In response, Agent Lightning v1.0 introduces Collocated Async RL, which lets rollout and model updates share the same set of GPUs. Once the system has collected enough rollouts, the update begins: the API Gateway pauses accepting new requests and waits for requests already in progress to finish, and rollout resumes after the update completes. The entire state transition is transparent to the external agent harness. In experiments, this approach achieved about a 2x end-to-end speedup over synchronous RL while using fewer GPUs than conventional asynchronous RL (Figure 3). Collecting enough rollouts means running many agents at once, which consumes substantial CPU, memory, and compute resources. Other Harnessed Agentic RL frameworks often host those agents on commercial sandbox services such as Modal Sandbox or E2B, where cost climbs quickly with scale. Instead, Agent Lightning v1.0 runs them as standard Kubernetes jobs, reusing existing self-managed clusters, cloud Kubernetes, or local infrastructure (Figure 4). Existing compute resources are used more efficiently, large rollouts cost less, and the whole pipeline stays open source and reproducible. To test the approach, researchers built a full pipeline on SWE-smith, mini-SWE-agent, and Qwen3.5-9B, covering data cleaning, environment construction, reward-hacking safeguards, and RL training. The training set holds about 6,000 samples and needs no large-scale compute. RL training alone raised Qwen3.5-9B from 41.8% to 56.4% on SWE-bench Verified, a gain of 14.6 percentage points. The coding agent experiments further confirm the earlier analysis of two challenges: advantage calculation and loss normalization. Compared with sample-level handling, rollout-level advantage combined with rollout-level normalization achieves a higher validation reward and keeps policy entropy more stable during training (Figure 5). The post Agent Lightning v1.0: A 3,500-Line Lightweight Agentic RL Framework for Training Agents with Real Harnesses appeared first on Microsoft Research .

title: Set Budgets and Alerts for Cloud Data Warehouse Costs
abstract: Every analytics team has been here: a month-end invoice arrives, and a single SQL warehouse has blown through its budget, maybe a compute left running overnight, maybe an ad hoc one that auto-scaled to serve 80 Tableau users during a quarterly review. The cost is real, but the frustration runs deeper: nobody knew until it was too late. Proactive cost management flips that model. Instead of forensic bill analysis after the fact, you set guardrails before a dollar is spent - budgets are tied to warehouses, teams, or BI workloads. Alerts that fire at the thresholds you choose, and dashboards that surface usage trends in real time, all on the Databricks Data & AI Platform . If you're mid-migration from an on-premises system or another cloud data warehouse, now is the moment to put that governance in place. Data warehousing workloads present unique cost challenges. SQL warehouses serve interactive, human-driven workloads (BI dashboards, ad hoc analysis, embedded analytics) where demand is unpredictable and bursty. A single executive all-hands that triggers 200 simultaneous dashboard refreshes can spike costs in minutes. Most organizations start their FinOps journey the same way: someone downloads last month's usage CSV, opens a pivot table, and starts asking questions. This approach breaks down for four reasons: Proactive cost management — attribution, budgets, alerts, dashboards, and optimization — addresses all five. Before setting up budgets, choose the right warehouse type. SQL Serverless warehouses are Databricks’ recommended option for most workloads. They start in seconds, scale down the moment queries finish, and let Intelligent Workload Management allocate compute for you, so you pay only for actual query execution, not idle readiness. If you're migrating from a legacy cloud data warehouse, this is a major shift. Most legacy platforms charge for always-on compute or require manual scaling decisions. Serverless removes that entire class of cost mistakes. Lumen Technologies saw this firsthand: Migrating two essential telecom systems from an on-premises data warehouse to SQL Serverless reduced compute costs by 30 -40% and increased query speed by 90%. The system now automatically scales to handle approximately 7 GB every 10 minutes, with Serverless removing the "always-on tax" typically associated with bursty, real-time workloads. The framework consists of five pillars. The first four make your spend visible; the fifth is what actually brings it down: You can't manage what you can't attribute, and with warehouses that means two levels: the warehouse itself and the individual query. One tells you which warehouse spent the money; the other tells you who inside it did. Level 1: Tagging the warehouse SQL warehouses support custom tags as key:value pairs that propagate to system.billing.usage, linking every DBU consumed to a team, project, or cost centre. Tagging works the same way for every warehouse type — Classic, Pro, and Serverless are all tagged at the warehouse level, so you learn one pattern and apply it everywhere. Set tags in the UI under SQL Warehouses > your warehouse > Edit > Tags, or create the warehouse through the REST API: Apply at least three dimensions: team (who owns it), cost center (who pays), and use case (BI serving, ad hoc, scheduled refresh). There isn't a native policy today that enforces warehouse tags, so anyone can create an untagged one. Build enforcement into your provisioning process instead — create warehouses with Terraform, Declarative Automation Bundles, or the REST API with tags in the definition, and treat the UI as the exception. The attribution-gap query later in this post catches whatever slips through. Warehouse tags tell you a warehouse cost $4,000 last month. They don't tell you that 60% of it came from a single Power BI dashboard refreshing every 15 minutes. That gap matters because warehouses are shared — one BI warehouse serves dozens of dashboards, several dbt models, and a stream of ad hoc queries. Query tags (Public Preview) close it by attaching business context to individual SQL statements: The tags land in the query_tags column of system.query.history (Public Preview), alongside executed_by and statement_id, so you can group spend by dashboard, model, or cost centre rather than by warehouse. Some tools set these for you: starting with dbt-databricks 1.11.0, model queries are automatically tagged with the dbt model name, and Power BI passes workspace and dataset identifiers through the ADBC driver. Two caveats: query tags apply to SQL warehouse queries only, and because they live in query history rather than billing data, you join the two yourself to get per-query cost. Before writing any SQL, check the Cost page in Governance Hub (Beta) — an account-level view of spend, cost drivers, budgets, and tagging coverage, and the quickest way to see how much of your usage is attributable at all. An account admin enables it from the account console's Previews page. In the Account Console, go to Usage > Budgets , click Add budget , and configure: cto@co.com, finops@company.com The key pattern is layered budgets: team-level budgets for accountability, plus an account-wide budget as a safety net that catches anything that slips through. Keep in mind that budgets are a monitoring mechanism, not a hard cap. They don't stop usage or prevent charges, so your bill can still exceed the amount. The goal is awareness and rapid response, not shutoffs that could break a production dashboard mid-refresh. GetYourGuide tested this directly: consolidating all their Looker workloads onto SQL Serverless lowered BI serving costs by ~20% and sped queries 35%, even though the team had expected Classic clusters to be cheaper. Warehouse-type choice is a budgeting decision worth re-validating, not a one-time call. Click any budget to see current spend vs. target, remaining budget, and a day-by-day burn-rate visualisation. For data warehousing, this chart is especially revealing: Budgets tell you where you stand. Alerts tell you when to act. When you create a budget, add email recipients who are notified when spending exceeds the budget amount. Zero code is needed. For threshold-based alerting, create Databricks SQL Alerts that query `system.billing.usage` directly. Here are the patterns that matter most: This is the pattern teams get the most value from. Instead of alerting after the breach, it projects month-end spend and fires before that projection crosses your budget while you still have time to act: Schedule this every four hours and route to Slack or email. It gives teams days to react (right-size a warehouse, optimize an expensive query, defer a batch) before the budget is breached. Materialized view refresh costs are the ones teams miss most often, because they bill as serverless pipeline usage rather than warehouse usage. A view set to refresh every 15 minutes against a source that updates twice a day spends the difference for no benefit. Match the refresh schedule to how often the underlying data actually changes, then watch the pipeline spend directly: Alerts are point-in-time triggers. Dashboards give continuous context. Databricks provides pre-built usage dashboards that account admins can import into any Unity Catalog-enabled workspace. These cover spend trends, top-N analysis, tag filtering, and per-warehouse drill-downs. For custom monitoring, two queries are particularly useful: Untagged SQL usage is your attribution gap, warehouse spend that can't be traced to any team. Drive it to zero. Raiffeisen Bank International built its own cost-monitoring and forecasting platform directly on Databricks system tables, with per-warehouse, per-user, and per-workload visibility. The payoff was cultural as much as technical: 3-4x faster workloads and, more importantly, when teams can see their own spend and are expected to explain it, behaviour changes without mandates. The first four pillars are about seeing your spending.

title: Now GA: Building permission-aware Databricks Apps with on-behalf-of-user authorization
abstract: Databricks Apps lets developers build and deploy data and AI applications directly on the Databricks platform, from interactive dashboards and operational tools to custom AI agents. Now generally available, on-behalf-of-user (OBO) authorization makes it possible to build apps that deliver personalized, permission-aware experiences without reimplementing data-governance rules in application code. When an app calls supported Databricks APIs with OBO, it acts using the signed-in user’s identity: Unity Catalog enforces that user’s existing data permissions, including row filters and column masks, and API scopes limit the operations the app can perform on the user’s behalf. Apps can continue to use their dedicated service principal for app-owned operations, such as reading shared configuration or writing application metrics. For example, a sales-insights assistant can answer questions using only the accounts and fields a salesperson is authorized to access, without giving the app broad SQL or workspace-administration capabilities. When designing an app, ask: Whose permissions should govern this particular operation? Databricks Apps supports two complementary authorization models: app authorization and user authorization. App authorization uses the app’s dedicated service principal and is appropriate for app-owned operations or experiences that should return the same result to every user. User authorization uses the signed-in user’s identity when that user’s permissions should govern an operation. Most production apps can use both models, choosing the appropriate identity for each request path. See Configure authorization in a Databricks app . Query data filtered by the current user API scope: sql:restricted-query The query runs as the user and is limited to read-only SQL queries. Read shared configuration or metadata The app’s service principal provides consistent access. Run background jobs or maintenance Background work should not depend on a user session. Perform a user-triggered action on governed data The API scope required for that operation The action is evaluated using the initiating user’s permissions. Combine shared behavior with user-specific data Separate API scopes for each user-authorized capability Use an app client for app-owned operations and a user client for governed operations. Consider an app that answers questions such as: How are my accounts performing this quarter, and what explains the change? The app needs to: This is a natural fit for user authorization. The app passes the requesting user’s forwarded access token to the SQL connector, and Databricks evaluates the query using that user’s existing warehouse and Unity Catalog permissions. A regional manager might see only accounts in their region, while a national leader sees all regions, without the app recreating those rules in code. When administrators update Unity Catalog policies, subsequent app requests reflect those changes. The user’s permission determines which data the query can return. The next design decision is what the app is allowed to do on the user’s behalf with the forwarded user token. The sales-insights assistant needs to execute read-only queries. It does not need broad SQL access to manage resources or perform other SQL operations. For that reason, it should request sql:restricted-query rather than the broader sql scope. sql:restricted-query allows the app to execute read-only SQL queries. It does not allow the app to perform other SQL operations. This creates a better match between the app’s product behavior and its authorization boundary: the app can read governed data for analysis, but it cannot use the user’s identity as a broad SQL operating credential. If the app also invokes Genie or Unity Gateway on a user’s behalf, request only the corresponding scopes, such as genie or ai-gateway. Do not request files, model-serving, or vector-search unless the app actually uses those capabilities. Scopes are a capability ceiling, not a grant of data access. The app must have the appropriate API scope, and the user must still have permission to access the target resource. See Scope-based security and privilege escalation . Configure user authorization in the Databricks UI or in a Declarative Automation Bundle . For a read-only analytics assistant, the app can declare: Note: The API scope is part of the app’s declared user-authorization configuration. It does not grant access to a SQL warehouse or Unity Catalog data. The requesting user must still be allowed to use the target SQL warehouse and have the required Unity Catalog privileges on the data being queried. When a user first accesses a user-authorized app, Databricks prompts them to consent to the requested API scopes. Databricks forwards the current user’s access token in the x-forwarded-access-token HTTP header. The app should retrieve that token for the request that needs user-context access and pass it to the SQL connector. The following example uses Flask and the Databricks SQL Connector for Python to make the token flow explicit. If you build the app with Databricks AppKit, apply the same authorization principle: use the user-context client or request-time identity for user-specific operations, and keep app-owned operations on the app identity. Note: The forwarded token is short-lived and per-request. The app reads it on each request and never stores it across requests or in a session. The important difference from app authorization is that the connector receives the forwarded user token through access_token. The sql:restricted-query API scope limits the app to the read-only SQL capability it needs, while Unity Catalog determines which rows and columns that user can actually access. See Query with user authorization . Developers specify which API scopes their app needs. Workspace administrators can control which API scopes app developers are allowed to add to apps in the workspace. That policy lets teams build read-only analytics and AI experiences while preventing apps from requesting broader or unrelated capabilities. An app developer cannot expand the app’s authorization beyond the workspace’s configured API-scope boundary. This gives organizations two levels of control: Workspace administrators configure this allowlist under Settings > Development > Apps . The setting defaults to all supported APIs, can be narrowed to selected API scopes, or can be set to None to disable user authorization. See Restrict user authorization scopes . Account administrators can add scopes even when those scopes are not included in the workspace allowlist. If an administrator later removes an allowed scope, apps already running with that scope can continue running, but they cannot be started, deployed, or updated until the non-allowed scope is removed. Many useful apps need both authorization models. The sales insights assistant might use: It is advisable to make that identity boundary explicit in application code instead of creating one generic client and reusing it everywhere. Separate dependencies, names, and tests help prevent an app credential from being used for a user-specific path or a user token from being retained for background work. If a request requires user authorization and the forwarded token is missing, fail closed rather than silently switching to the app’s service principal. Otherwise, the app could return a response that looks valid but was generated with different permissions. That is why query_as_user in the example above starts with require_user_token instead of handling the missing header inline. Custom agents deployed on Databricks Apps can use the same model. Initialize the user-scoped workspace client inside the request-time invoke or stream handler—not at application startup—because the forwarded user token is available only during an active user request. Use app authorization for shared resources and background operations. See Authentication for agents .

title: How to Repoint dbt ETL Pipelines to Databricks
abstract: • Learn how to repoint your existing dbt project from any source warehouse to Databricks with minimal code changes • Walk through the practical steps: adapter setup, namespace mapping, SQL dialect differences, development workflow, and production scheduling with Lakeflow Jobs • Understand how to validate outputs model by model and cut over safely More teams are running their dbt transformations on Databricks Lakehouse : an open platform with no lock-in, unified pipelines, built-in Unity Catalog governance, and strong price/performance. Your dbt project works: models compile, tests pass, and your transformation logic lives in version-controlled SQL and YAML, not hardwired into any one warehouse. dbt’s open adapter framework is designed for exactly this decoupling, so moving from one cloud data warehouse to another is mostly a matter of changing the adapter and connection config plus a few dialect tweaks - not rewriting your DAG or business logic. Databricks delivers on that with the co-engineered dbt-databricks adapter, open lakehouse storage ( Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg™ ), Unity Catalog , and Lakeflow Jobs that give you an open, unified platform where dbt runs with built-in governance and strong price/performance from day one, making it a great place to run your dbt workloads . That’s why more than 3,000 organizations already run dbt on Databricks. If you’ve been evaluating a move, the good news is you don’t have to rebuild your project. This post walks through how to repoint a working dbt project to Databricks by swapping the adapter and profile, handling a handful of SQL differences, and keeping your transformation logic inside dbt. A recurring challenge with data warehouse migration projects is trying to move everything at once, which can lead to delays and bottlenecks. A better approach is to start with the transformation layer, which is a fast way to unlock cost savings from a migration. dbt projects are already modular and testable. That makes them ideal candidates for an incremental migration. When you repoint dbt to Databricks, you get: Scope: This guide covers repointing your dbt transformation layer only. It assumes your source data is already in Databricks — landed as Delta or Iceberg tables and registered in Unity Catalog — and that your catalogs and schemas exist. Migrating the data itself and setting up Unity Catalog are separate efforts; see the Databricks migration guides and Lakebridge for those. Before you start, make sure you have: The model we will be migrating in this example is a standard analytics fact table built on top of two source models: orders and order_items . It aggregates order-level data to calculate total revenue and compiles a list of products sold for every individual transaction from the past year. This model uses several common SQL dialect patterns , such as regexp_substr , div0 and object_construct , which often differ between data warehouses, making it a great example. Once you see how to handle these patterns here, you can apply the same approach to every other model in your project. This part covers the one-time migration work which involves installing the adapter, mapping namespaces, and handling dialect differences. Install the dbt-databricks adapter The dbt-databricks adapter is the bridge between your dbt project and the Databricks Lakehouse warehouse. It translates dbt's compiled SQL into Databricks-compatible queries. (dbt Platform users: select "Databricks" as the connection type in a new environment as detailed in the dbt docs - the adapter is installed automatically.) Add a Databricks target to `profiles.yml`. Keep your existing target intact; you'll need it during validation. Add a second target alongside it: You should see: Connection test: [OK connection ok]. If you still cannot connect, follow the connection troubleshooting steps in the Databricks + dbt integration guide and the dbt Databricks profile reference . Pro Tip: http_path determines whether queries run on a SQL warehouse (recommended for dbt) or an all-purpose cluster. SQL warehouses offer better price/performance for SQL-heavy workloads. Databricks uses a three-level namespace: catalog.schema.table . Update the sources.yml entries that fct_orders reads from: Update schema.yml to include tests Pro Tip: If you skip database: , queries land in the workspace's default catalog. Set it explicitly. Now run dbt compile for the model: Our fct_orders model produced 3 compilation errors as detailed below, all dialect-related. This is expected and while these three are representative of the dialect issues most projects hit, they aren't the whole story: larger migrations also run into incremental-model strategies, snapshots, and semi-structured functions with no direct equivalent. We intentionally use an example model that relies on dialect-specific patterns like REGEXP_SUBSTR with positional parameters, DIV0 for safe division, and OBJECT_CONSTRUCT for JSON building - the kind of functions that differ between warehouses. That way, the initial dbt run errors become a guide through the conversion process, showing you how to turn these into portable macros and Databricks-friendly SQL so you can apply the same fixes across the rest of your project. To demonstrate, we will walk you through each error, the root cause, and the fix. Before diving into the errors, a note on portability: where a function has a portable equivalent, dbt's cross-database macros (the dbt.* namespace) let you write it once so it compiles on any warehouse — worth adopting as you standardize. We'll walk through each error and its fix, then show how to automate the conversion across a large project. Databricks follows Apache SQL dialect and only supports 2 parameters for REGEXP_SUBSTR Fix: use Databricks’ native regexp_extract() function You could also let the Genie Code make this conversion for you, fixing dialect gaps like this is exactly what it's good at. We'll do all three by hand so you can see what's changing. Root cause: some warehouses use DIV0 to return 0 instead of throwing an error when dividing by zero. Fix : add dbt_utils to your packages and use its built-in safe_divide function Cannot resolve routine `object_construct` Fix: Use the Databricks named_struct function Compiles successfully. Total dialect changes for this model: dbt_utils package installed (for safe division), regexp_substr call converted to regexp_extract , div0 call replaced with dbt_utils.safe_divide() , object_construct call converted to named_struct . Fixing three functions by hand is easy. A real dbt project has hundreds or thousands of models, and these dialect gaps are exactly what AI tooling closes automatically. The Genie Code converts dialect-specific SQL and handles these fixes right in the editor, so you spend your time reviewing the conversions instead of writing each one. With compile green, execute the model and any tests that exist: Both model build and tests pass. Pro Tip: A green dbt run proves the SQL executes. Now, we need to reconcile the outputs across legacy warehouse and Databricks. Use dbt-audit-helper to compare row-by-row. Compare fct_orders across both warehouses. In analyses/compare_fct_orders.sql : Run it against Databricks (assuming you've replicated the legacy output into Databricks for the comparison, or run a cross-warehouse comparison): Note: These examples cover the most common patterns, but are not exhaustive. For any additional mismatches (e.g. string trimming, collation, or custom UDF behavior), set summarize=false to materialize sample rows, inspect a few primary keys where in_a and in_b differ, fix the model or macro, and rerun until you get a 100% match. In our run: fct_orders matched exactly. Instead of maintaining a separate orchestration layer for dbt, you can run dbt alongside upstream ingestion and downstream actions in a single pipeline with Lakeflow Jobs.

title: “Software is over”: Bold AI developer takes aim at Adobe with open source clones
abstract: For a while, those hoping to avoid the difficulty and expense of dealing with Adobe's Creative Suite have been able to use several free and/or open-source alternatives that replicate some or all of those capabilities. Now, one developer is using AI-powered reverse engineering to mimic the look, feel, and functionality of Adobe's well-known software with what he hopes will soon be perfect fidelity. Artcraft got its start last year as a "controllable AI for artists" that allows for precise post-generation editing of AI-crafted images and videos. Over the weekend, though, the brand debuted its pivot to a suite of seven open source apps recreating the user interface and tools found in Adobe's Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, After Effects, InDesign, and Acrobat Pro. In announcing those new apps on Reddit earlier this week, software developer Brandon Thomas said he used Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 to create "clean-room replacements" for Adobe's closed source software in Rust (with WebAssembly versions available for use in a browser). And while commenters on Hacker News and elsewhere have taken pains to point out the new software's many current shortcomings, Thomas make the grandiose promise that the current "super early alpha" state will soon lead to something just as functional as anything Adobe has ever put out.

title: Fraudster jailed for using 10K bots and AI songs to outstream Taylor Swift
abstract: After pleading guilty, a 54-year-old North Carolina man, Michael Smith, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for using artificial intelligence to generate songs for a scheme that stole millions from music streaming platforms. In a press release Tuesday, the US Department of Justice said that Smith is the first American criminally charged with AI-assisted streaming fraud. First charged in 2024, Smith successfully ran the scheme for seven years without detection. Starting in 2017, Smith began using fake email accounts and “fraudulently obtained debit cards” to create “thousands of fraudulent accounts” on services including Amazon Music, Apple Music, Spotify, and YouTube Music, the DOJ said. He then employed software that pushed the bots to continuously stream songs that he claimed to own, which the DOJ said were AI-generated. By his arrest in 2024, he had created “hundreds of thousands of AI-generated songs,” then dispersed billions of automated streams among them so that the bots could avoid raising any red flags by all targeting the same song at once. All together, the fake songs generated substantially more streams than some of the most popular artists today, however. According to the DOJ, in a glaring example from April 2023, Smith’s fake songs were fraudulently streamed 80.9 million times during that month, while Taylor Swift’s entire catalog only got 9.3 million streams during the same time period.

title: Mistral says "Le Chonk" can challenge the best AI models
abstract: As tensions mount over who gets access to top-end artificial intelligence , French company Mistral has released a new freely available model that it claims can compete with the very best from the US and China. The new 1 trillion-parameter model, Mistral Large 4—nicknamed Le Chonk—can be used and customized by anyone. It’s currently available in preview, with a final version to follow by the end of the month. Though Le Chonk is built to compete with leading general-purpose models, it’s optimized specifically for coding and cyberdefense, as well as tasks particular to manufacturing, finance, electrical engineering, and other niches. “There are a lot of areas where the other labs will not focus that much,” Guillaume Lample, cofounder and chief scientist at Mistral, tells WIRED. “There are so many domains in which you can improve models.” Mistral presents Le Chonk as by far the most capable open-weight model developed outside of China, and “very, very close” to some proprietary models. Whereas Chinese labs have been accused by the US government of abusing distillation—the training of a smaller model on the outputs of a larger one—to close the performance gap with OpenAI and Anthropic, Mistral claims to have trained its model from scratch. It’s already considerably cheaper for businesses to run open-weight models, which cost only as much as the compute they consume. By reducing the performance gap on leading proprietary models and providing a competitive alternative to releases from China, Mistral says, Le Chonk will eliminate the few remaining reasons a business might hesitate to choose open source. “Mistral is still in the race of getting the best model,” Lample says. “This is the main message.” With less capital and fewer compute resources than OpenAI and Anthropic, Mistral has generally lagged behind on model performance, revenue, and the frequency of releases. While the US labs charge a premium for access to their proprietary, closed-weight models, Mistral generates revenue by charging pay-as-you-go fees for running models through its cloud and deploying engineers to help customers tune models to their specific needs. Recently, however, the French lab has been on a hot streak: In September, it raised a $3.3 billion funding round at a $24 billion valuation, the largest ever raise by a European tech company. Its earnings have reportedly increased 20-fold in the last year or so.

title: Google rolls out improved SynthID AI content detector, now available globally
abstract: Every piece of AI content from Google's Gemini models has a hidden SynthID label, which makes it very difficult to pass the content off as authentic . SynthID has also gotten buy-in from other major AI players, but actually checking for those invisible watermarks has been a convoluted process. It's going to be a little easier going forward, though. Google has announced that its SynthID detector now supports watermarks from all its partners, and it's available for anyone to use on a new dedicated website. SynthID is an invisible signal encoded in the pixels of AI-generated images and videos, and in the waveform of AI audio. Google says Gemini alone has integrated SynthID with over 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio. Until now, the only way for those outside of Google's trusted tester program to check for SynthID was to ask Gemini. This is rather clunky, and the model's output could sometimes be confusing when you just wanted a simple "yes" or "no." Now you can cut Gemini out of the loop. Starting today, you can go to the new SynthID.com website to check a piece of content for an AI watermark. A major limitation of Google's previous detector was that it only checked for Google's version of SynthID. Even though ChatGPT images, for example, have SynthID, they wouldn't be flagged in Google's detector. That's no longer a problem.

title: The Curve Bends You
abstract: That is not the worst possible plan. But it is close. Since before the transformer, we have warned that the most suicidal thing you could do would be to ask your AI to do your alignment homework, and automate the process. Alignment is complex and interacts deeply with every aspect of the world, and is one of the hardest possible things for an AI to get right even if it means maximally well and is itself functionally aligned. Mistakes get amplified up the chain, you get exactly what you optimized for, and you are rather doomed. Never go full RSI. Yet, now more than ever, this seems to be the plan: The good news is, most people realize this is at best a no-good terrible plan and would prefer a better one. The bad news is that some people still think this is a plan that, while not great, still has a solid chance of working, with only some small (e.g. 10%) chance of getting us all killed, as opposed to being probably suicidal. The other bad news is, not only does no one have a better plan, the labs are terrified that things are going so fast they cannot even execute step 1 of this non-plan. The good news is, they are trying to do something about that. Pacing the frontier. So that we at least can hope to reasonably execute the not-plan. Once again, the government is actively getting in the way for now, although we have hope that this could swiftly change. Or maybe, just maybe, we can not execute the not-plan. Which would be better. Two years ago, at a new conference called The Curve , the worried and e/accs were brought together for discussions, debates, presentations and a tabletop exercise. Last year, the odds were against us and the situation was grim , as the conference transitioned to an SF vs. DC profile. The differences of year one had been some mix of reconciled and overcome by events, and we strived to at least make some progress against a government actively determined to stop any attempts to not die and labs determined to sprint ahead. This year, in its third iteration, The Curve found people in good spirits. In some ways we were filled with hope. In others everyone is terrified. Hence the hope. Thanks to a combination of the HuggingFace Incident, Jacob Coxon and various surrounding events, the lab employees are freaking out, the labs are speaking up and the public and DC are waking up fast. Welcome back. It’s good to see you again. Hopefully we get to keep meeting like this. The big change for year three is that AI is now sufficiently Serious Business , on the DC side and also on the San Francisco side, that the whole conference defaulted to Chatham House. Chatham House rules mean you can use and report what you learned, but you cannot share who you got it from, nor their affiliations. That makes things tricky. I will share what I can given that restriction, and I have tasked my editor Opus 5.5 with ensuring that I am within those rules. The Curve Season 3 was sufficiently good that part of me wished it was worse. When you go to a great conference, you see opportunity everywhere. There are sessions you want to attend, nay that you need to attend. There are people you want to talk to, nay that you need to talk to. That’s a lot of pressure. You must face the FOMO. You can’t stop, won’t stop. Whereas you know what I really, really needed? A vacation. I’m tired, man. I don’t know if you’ve noticed, but September was a hell of a month. Thus, when I looked at the list of people coming, it was a mix of ‘wow that’s an amazing list’ and ‘oh no that is an amazing list.’ Most of them did not disappoint. Yet, alas, I cannot say the thing I said last year, that every substantive conversation I had made me smarter. Many very much did, or at least better informed. Others did not do this. They made me feel scared, or frustrated, or disappointed, with echoes of conversations and years past. The Eternal September remains upon us, even in 2026. The more things change, and progress towards the inevitable, the less some people are inclined to update even their talking points. I can take it, but I wish to not do so. Part of this is that when you invite ‘higher level’ people, they are not as situationally aware. There were also people who should have moved past this, who hadn’t. There was still opportunity everywhere, for those willing to use Lighthaven norms and walk away from the places it was lacking. I also deliberately spent a bunch of time, especially on Sunday evening, not trying to maximize my impact or knowledge gathering, without any agenda except relaxing and having a good time. I think I did maybe 75% as much of that as I should have. The bulk of people put AI at 10, with only one high 8. As I put it last year, if you were situationally aware enough to show up, you are aware of the situation. The patch at the bottom was to illustrate what ‘most Americans’ think, not answers by attendees. Then this year, we did it again: This is substantial backsliding, despite AI having radically advanced in the past year. There are now at least five dots in the high 8s, and a lot more 9s. Astra summarized the changes this way. This is a huge drop. Situational awareness, in this sense, was down 0.41 points, if you max the scale at 10. At this point, I don’t see any answer other than 10+ as defensible, if you are actually paying attention and interpret this as a forward projection. That’s why we are all here having this conversation. My Twitter followers are doing worse, but also have more of an excuse : Last year, there were estimates of how long until various things happened. That’s hard to read, so [the medians are approximately]: Where are we now? Here are the ones with clear updates available: Question #1 is up to roughly 50% right now, unless you count code that is thrown away in which case we are likely above 90% already. Claude suggests we are on track for 2028 on this. I disagree and think this is clearly either 2026 or 2027. Question #4 was settled yesterday, with at least one instant Fields Medal , and also by solving Navier-Stokes. 2026. Question #5 is going to be close. MEDVi is more than a billion dollars from two people. But we’re not strictly there yet from what I could find. This year’s questions were different. AI training a superior successor on its own is full RSI. The majority of people expected this to happen within two years and a lot of them expect it within six months. It’s hard to reconcile this with ‘only a 9’ on the Richter Scale. There are some other fun differences of opinion here as well. Once you get past two years, everything gets tied up in whether we are in full RSI-takeoff-singularity mode. Two years seems about right for email, as does five years for robots which is mostly a hardware scaling question. The other survey questions were new this year. Attendees expected a wide variety of different things and were remarkably optimistic given the situation. Many are in denial, which goes hand in hand with ‘only a 9.’ As readers will know, I think Doom v1 is the most likely of these outcomes, and indeed is over 50%, and I expect the second most likely outcome is Utopia. Whereas a lot of people expect something else to happen, most often this mysterious ‘normal technology’ scenario. As with many such conferences, there was the standard set of tracks, plus one bonus. I skipped other tracks, and related discussions, due to not seeing opportunity. Last year I noted that many talks started with the assumption, explicit or otherwise, that AI would remain a ‘normal technology.’ I avoided those talks. This year I believe a few of those talks still existed, and indeed a lot more people claim to believe this. Nor did I try to convince the doubters. Several of the ‘classic doubters’ were in attendance, including some that are consistently in good faith. I could have easily sought them out. I am not going to convince them, I have learned, and I am confident they will not convince me.

title: Childhood and Education #21: Grades and Standards
abstract: First you get to college via the wrong metrics, as previously discussed in #12 . Then things get easier. I’m still digging out from under everything that happened the four days I was gone. Normal AI posting should resume tomorrow, likely with a report from the conference. The declines in NAEP scores and other tests seem to be concentrated on the weakest students. The bottom of the distribution is falling through the floor and the rest is mostly holding up. This does not match anecdotal reports coming out of schools, which suggest widespread declines, although those are presumably untrustworthy and it’s traditional to think children are in general getting dumber. That doesn’t mean they aren’t but we need systematic evidence. This really would be far worse than I think if it was true. Tyler Cowen: It is worse than you think: Of 360,000 children aged 15 in Zambia only five (not 5%, 5 total) could read at “globally proficient levels.” I mean, in addition to this meaning essentially college-level reading skills, it’s very obviously not true. The statement makes absolutely no sense, and is based at best on an Obvious Nonsense theoretical distribution of scores. Oli (top comment): There are two private schools in the capital, Lusaka, American International School of Lusaka and International School of Lusaka. 25% of ISL students get a score of 40+ in ‘international baccalaureate’ exam with an average of 35 . Aisl gets an average of 34 . I know friendship groups who were in the same school year at these schools who can all read and write well. Your periodic reminder . See this study , also this one and this one . SAT scores and other objective measures fight income inequality in college admissions . Holistic admissions make it worse . But then everyone already knew that. A paper from Raj Chetty, David Deming and John Friedman brings the math . Gerry Tan: If you *only* used SAT to admit to elite colleges, share of admits from top 1% income falls 15.8% → 9.9% and representation from <$200k rises by +8.8%, with no reduction in post-college outcomes. It’s ‘holistic review’ and ‘ban SAT’ policy that allows the most wealthy and powerful to virtue signal while getting an edge. Paper Abstract: The high-income admissions advantage at Ivy-Plus colleges is driven by three factors: (1) preferences for children of alumni, (2) weight placed on non-academic credentials, and (3) athletic recruitment. The three factors that give children from high-income families an admissions advantage are uncorrelated or negatively correlated with post-college outcomes, whereas academic credentials such as SAT/ACT scores are highly predictive of post-college success. Non-academic credentials, including most athletic slots (since most are not the popular and accessible sports like basketball or football), end up largely being manufactured by the wealthy by spending money and performing class. As commentator Naveen says, the main flaw in the SAT/ACT is that they run into big time ceiling effects, and can’t differentiate top 1% from top 0.1% or top 0.01%. There is a very easy and obvious fix for that, which are academic credentials that do differentiate at that level. What, like it’s hard? Even if we can’t do better than this, and we have to do exactly zero innovation, we can give the students eyeing Ivy+ level colleges the GRE or the LSAT or the AIME. Check their AP scores. And so on. One main problem with SAT and ACT scores is that they max out. If you’re trying to get into Harvard, you have a 2400 or 36, but mostly so does everyone else. There is a simple solution to this, which is to extend the SAT and ACT so the top score is higher, and the toughest questions are a lot tougher, and no one ever gets a perfect score. This only impacts the very top directly, but it also means one can aspire to that elite and make it count, shifting incentives. There are other standardized tests like AP exams, and in theory one could jump ahead and take a GRE test in 11th grade, but in practice these don’t do the job. My actual belief matches Paul Graham, that this is all on purpose , as part of the War on Education. We don’t want to give smarter or more knowledgeable students a big advantage, so we make it hard to see. Holistic admissions creates incentives to look good by holistic standards, as teens scramble to optimize their every moment, including an increasing emphasis on eating everyone’s summers, to score every point they can and convey a ‘story’ to college admissions. That includes choosing that ‘story,’ including what you aim to study, by junior year of high school at the latest . That’s all in addition to rising pressures to engage in active lying , literal live kayfabe performances and preference falsification, or else. Some even start tiny non-profits, which is a complete waste of time. I think pressuring kids to volunteer for ‘community service’ or at nonprofits to graduate high school or sell themselves to colleges is analogous to indentured servitude and we should look upon it in horror. Legally mandated highly ineffective altruism mixed with child slavery. And this is if anything stupider and worse. Marc Porter Magee : The kids know this is a meaningless exercise. Their parents know it too. Even the college admissions teams must know it. And yet it rolls forward, getting more intense each year. Having started a nonprofit, I feel confident in saying incentivizing children to do it to gain an edge in a college application is a huge waste of everyone’s time and money. It usually takes a year just to get your IRS determination letter. There is a ton of overhead involved, which isn’t worth it unless you are raising a ton of money over a long period of time. How about start by volunteering somewhere you believe in? Should kids be pushed to file with the IRS to take in $1,000 in donations to give sunscreen to 250 people? What exactly are we incentivizing here, the trappings of founding something? This isn’t a question of kids having a summer job or volunteering. It’s telling kids that’s not good enough. They can’t just volunteer, they have to start a nonprofit. They can’t just have a summer job, they have to found a company. I too have started a 501c(3) nonprofit, Balsa Research . I believe in the work we’re doing, and also it’s very good for someone like me to have a 501c(3) in reserve in case I need one in a hurry for something else. But damn if it wasn’t an insane amount of overhead, in terms of the money and time and work required to have it exist at all. Doing this as a high schooler is mainly a way to learn to hate government red tape. Wilterson Witzky da Silva : i do think the Gaokao is better than this I strongly agree that the Gaokao is a better way. It’s not first best, since it creates its own kind of all consuming zero sum competition, but it seems a lot more actually productive and less destructive. However, as noted in #12, you cannot simply fall back on SAT and GPA given the pressures that would put on GPA, even if you also throw in harder standardized tests. If you do holistic admissions, and people do something amazingly great, admit them. Hannah Cairo solved a 40-year-old mystery about how functions behave, called the Mizohata-Takeuchi conjecture, which she proved false while everyone else was trying to prove it was true. She was taking graduate classes in mathematics at Berkeley. So she skipped college and applied directly to graduate schools. Despite being obviously qualified, 6 out of 10 rejected her for not having a degree, and in 2 more cases she was admitted and then higher-ups in the administration overrode (!) the decision, leaving only University of Maryland and Johns Hopkins University. We had a similar situation in my high school class, where we had two supreme math talents on the IMO team. One, Alex, wanted to skip directly to graduate school.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5
abstract: As previously promised , here’s Anthropic’s new fast, low cost model: Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 . The previous Haiku, 4.5, was very much showing its age. It came out almost a year ago , and was priced at $1/million input and $5/million output—relatively expensive even back then, and a full 10x the price of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Luna , released last month. The new Haiku exactly matches the price of GPT-6 Luna—$0.10/$0.50—up to 100,000 tokens. Beyond 100,000 tokens the price increases 5x to $0.50/$2.50. Luna itself has a price increase at 272,000 tokens but only to $0.20/$0.75. Haiku 5.5 also uses a new, less generous tokenizer. My Claude Token Counter tool shows that the same long prompt uses around 1.25x as many tokens with Haiku 5.5 compared to Haiku 4.5, so there’s a hidden price increase there. If your workloads fit in 100,000 tokens, Haiku is the same price as Luna and reports higher benchmark scores. Above 100,000 tokens, Luna looks like a much better deal. The most recent release of llm-anthropic finally fixed it so I don’t need to ship a new version of that plugin for every new model. I tested the new model like this: Here are pelicans for low, medium, high, xhigh, and max . The new Haiku doesn’t let you disable reasoning, and defaults to medium . I got a good bicycle frame for everything beyond low . The low effort pelican cost 0.0936 cents and took 7 seconds. This max effort pelican took 5 minutes 9 seconds to generate, but still only cost me 3.3826 cents : For comparison, here’s the pelican I got a year ago from Haiku 4.5 (for 0.7583 cents —Haiku 4.5 did not support reasoning levels). It sucked at drawing pelicans: In addition to Haiku 5.5, Anthropic announced today that they are halving the price of cache reads for Sonnet 5.5. They’ve also added API credits to subscription plans: Second, this week, we’ll roll out a new monthly API credit to all Max and Team subscribers for use on the Claude Platform . Max 5x users will get $100 in credits per month, Max 20x users will get $200, and Team subscribers will receive up to $500, pooled across their users. Claiming this is pleasantly easy: navigate to Settings -> Billing and select the API organization that should benefit from the credits every month: The API credits exactly match the cost of the subscription itself. This is really generous—it makes it much easier for subscribers to use the API. Anthropic also let you disable auto-reload for the API, with the consequence that “API requests will stop when your balance runs out”—exactly what you want if you’re planning to burn through those API credits without risk of a nasty billing surprise . Note that the monthly credits do not roll over —use them or lose them. OpenAI still allow you to use your Codex subscription for personal API use, which works out as a better deal for heavy API users. This new credit scheme goes at least some way to overcoming that difference. This is Claude Haiku 5.5 by Simon Willison, posted on 7th October 2026 . title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 live blog
abstract: I’m at OpenAI DevDay today, in Fort Mason, San Francisco. Same as last year I’ll be live blogging the keynote and some other notes during the day. OpenAI gave me a free ticket and a seat in the “creator” area for the keynote. 09:27 I'm in the room for the keynote, which starts in half an hour. This year I vibe-coded a system for more easily adding photos to my live blog. I intended to do that using Codex Cloud (I built it on my phone on the way to the venue) but ran into problems with that and switched to Claude Code for web instead. 10:01 Sam Altman is on stage, welcoming us to DevDay. He promises "our best DevDay yet". 10:02 Showing features they've shipped that people asked for. Codex on Linux and Codex on your phone both got some applause. 10:03 Today, a product to feel like a "whole new way of working with AI". My guess is that it's a personal agent similar to Muse... 10:05 It does look very Muse-like. You get to pick its name, then it's represented by a cute blob-like avatar. (My Muse avatar is a pelican.) 10:06 This demo video includes a whole lot of voice interactions, presumably using GPT-Live or a new generation of that technology. 10:07 Dots are "powered by Astra". That would be an expensive default model! 10:08 A very ambitious use-case, migrating an API. I'm surprised that they went for such a code-heavy example so early on, I guess this is a developer audience. 10:09 Sam called Astra "our most aligned model", to allow you to trust your Dot with "as much responsibility as you are comfortable with". 10:09 "You also need a place four your team to collaborate with their Dots". So they are introducing ChatGPT Space . 10:10 These Spaces look like shared artifacts, maybe Google Docs meets the artifacts pattern. Sam Introduces Holly Li. These Spaces look like shared artifacts, maybe Google Docs meets the artifacts pattern. 10:11 Holly is talking through a scenario building fictional music app. Holly has a Dot called "Dottie", which has access to ChatGPT, Slack, Teams, and more. 10:12 This UI really does look like Meta's Muse agent, currently still at number one on the iOS App Store free list. 10:13 Live demo! "Dottie is having a slow morning" - we got a "still checking" and an embarrassing silent moment. 10:14 Now we're in ChatGPT Space. It has a Notion-style slash menu. 10:16 People at OpenAI started delegating to their Dots directly in Slack, which have their own identities in OpenAI Slack. I guess this is OpenAI's answer to Claude Tag . 10:17 "Dottie can use Codex on my laptop to build the app and launch it in the iPhone Simulator." 10:18 ChatGPT Pro and Enterprise customers get access to Dots today. 10:19 They're also building "specialist dots" for legal, finance, etc. They'll collaborate with enterprises on this, and are also doing a thing with Microsoft 365 around these. 10:20 "The second big part of today" is about platforms. Says says: Great models. Tools - access to the same tools used within OpenAI. And distribution. 10:21 People have been asking for GPT-6 Astra but cheaper and faster. Today they're launching GPT-6.1 Sol . 10:21 "Near-Astra level intelligence at a fifth of the price". 10:22 6.1 Sol is launching by today. 10:22 Also today: Ultrafast. 8x faster - up to 300 tokens/second.
